findings.description: The try block wraps self._flush(), so any exception from sink.write (I/O error, DB outage) is caught by `except Exception`. The whole batch is lost, because `batch` was already reset to [] before the flush. A single failed row number is recorded as rejected for what was really a batch-wide write failure. The loop keeps going, so a dead sink silently drops data. The report's loaded count does not include these rows and no error propagates, apart from TooManyRejected much later.
findings.suggestion: Only wrap parse_row in the try/except. Call self._flush outside it, so sink errors propagate. Catch specific parse exceptions (e.g. ValueError, KeyError) rather than Exception.
findings.title: Sink write failures are caught and recorded as a row rejection
